name: Pinotepa Nacional Mixtec
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Bradley, C. Henry 1970. A linguistic sketch of Jicaltepec Mixtec. SIL/Univ. of Oklahoma (the Pinotepa/Coast Mixtec variety); on archive.org as linguisticsketch0000chen
earlier_scan.note: archive.org copy is lending-restricted (access-restricted-item true; search-inside blocked); SIL Mexico resource pages return 403. Sketch phonology plausibly states stress.

new_statements.quote: The maximal syllable template is (C)V(C) with both the onset and the coda being optional. The only consonant that can appear in the coda is the glottal stop ( ꞌ ), and this consonant cannot appear in the onset. Syllables with a glottal stop in the coda appear only in the penultimate syllable. Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of polysyllabic content words; monosyllabic words (and the few bisyllabic function words) do not take stress.
new_statements.citation: Costello, Rachael A. 2014. Aspect and mood in Jicaltepec Mixtec. MA thesis, Graduate Institute of Applied Linguistics, Dallas (supervisor Michael Boutin). xiv+157 pp.
new_statements.locator: Ch. 3 'Overview of the grammar of Jicaltepec Mixtec', sec. 3.2 'Jicaltepec Mixtec phonology and orthography', pp. 24-25 (printed pagination; PDF pp. 38-39); the stress sentence is on p. 25
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable of polysyllabic content words. Since Mixtec content roots are bisyllabic couplets, this is the first syllable of the couplet; the glottal-stop coda is likewise restricted to that penultimate syllable. Monosyllabic words and the few bisyllabic function words are unstressed. The language is tonal (three level tones with a high/low allophone each, per Bradley 1970:13, with extensive sandhi); tone and stress are described independently.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllabic words and the few bisyllabic function words take no stress; no other exceptions given.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (content words); no statement about phrase-level stress or citation forms. Data are from the Mixtec of Santa María Jicaltepec (municipio Santiago Pinotepa Nacional), which Costello identifies with ISO mio / Ethnologue 'Pinotepa Nacional Mixtec'. The statement is a single sentence in an orthography-oriented phonology overview of an aspect/mood thesis, not a dedicated phonological analysis; Bradley 1970 (unreachable here) is the primary phonological description.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes the Mixtec of Santa María Jicaltepec (municipio Santiago Pinotepa Nacional, Oaxaca), which Costello (p. 20) equates with ISO 639-3 mio = Glottolog pino1237 'Pinotepa Nacional Mixtec' (also 'Jicaltepec Mixtec', 'Coastal Mixtec', INALI 'mixteco de Oaxaca de la costa oeste central'); MixteCoDB likewise files Santa María Jicaltepec (jica11) under pino1237. No separate glottocode exists for the Jicaltepec town variety. The unread Becerra Roldán 2018 thesis treats San Pedro Tulixtlahuaca, another town Glottolog places in pino1237.

The only consonant that can appear in the coda is the glottal stop ( ꞌ ), and this consonant cannot appear in the onset. Syllables with a glottal stop in the coda appear only in the penultimate syllable. sources.locator: Ch. 3 'Overview of the grammar of Jicaltepec Mixtec', sec. 3.2 'Jicaltepec Mixtec phonology and orthography', pp. 24-25 (printed pagination; PDF pp. 38-39); the stress sentence is on p. 25
sources.note: Sec. 3.2 (pp. 22-25) gives the consonant/vowel inventories, syllable template (C)V(C) with glottal-stop coda only in the penultimate syllable, and states that stress falls on the penultimate syllable of polysyllabic content words while monosyllabic words and the few bisyllabic function words are unstressed (p. 25). Sec. 3.3 (p. 26): three level tones per Bradley 1970:13, heavy tone sandhi; tone not represented in the orthographies. No mention of secondary stress.

sources.note: Nothing on stress; confirms that Santa María Jicaltepec (jica11), Santiago Pinotepa Nacional (pino11) and Pinotepa de Don Luis (pino12) are all treated as pino1237 / mio, i.e. the Costello variety belongs to this languoid.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page and langdoc list for pino1237 (10 references) — https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/pino1237
sources.note: Nothing on stress; gives alternate names (Coastal Mixtec, Lowland Jicaltepec Mixtec, Western Jamiltepec Mixtec, Mixteco de Pinotepa Nacional) and the reference list used above (adds Costello 2014, Josserand 1981/1983, Hollenbach 1991, Auderset et al. 2023 to the six descriptive refs).
No phonology content; cites only Bradley 1970 and Ethnologue 18.
